history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row is the same temple as seq 948 (id ucchi-pillayar-temple-trichy) - CSV row 948 'Ucchi Pillayar Temple, Tiruchirappalli' already documents this Rockfort complex. The Ucchi Pillayar Temple is the summit shrine of the Rockfort temple complex atop an 83-m rock in Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) - a granite outcrop estimated at ~3.8 billion years old, among the oldest rocks in the world. The rock was first cut by the Pallavas (rock-cut cave temples including the upper Lalitankura Pallavesvaram Griham of Mahendravarman I) and the temples were completed by the Nayaks of Madurai under the Vijayanagara Empire. Legend: this is where Ganesha ran from Vibhishana after establishing the Ranganatha idol at Srirangam. The complex holds three main shrines: Manikka Vinayakar at the foot, the large Thayumanaswamy (Shiva) temple mid-way, and Ucchi Pillayar at the summit reached by ~437-473 rock-cut steps. The hill was fortified and saw battles in the Carnatic Wars; the ancient cave temples are maintained by the ASI.

town_description: Tiruchirappalli (Trichy) is a major city in central Tamil Nadu on the Kaveri river. The Rockfort is its iconic central landmark; the temple complex is in the old-city area, about 2-3 km from Tiruchirappalli Junction. The summit view takes in the whole city, Srirangam and both rivers.
